name: @angular-modernizer/adapter-mcp

tools.name: analyze-project
tools.description: Analyze Angular projects to detect framework, architecture, layers, and technologies. counts holds the file and rule numbers, summary a short text; includeDetails returns the rule findings (maxResults and resultOffset page them).

rootPath.description: Root path of the project to analyze (auto-detected from .angular-modernizer.json if not provided)

includeDetails.description: Whether to include detailed analysis results

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (pagination)

resultOffset.description: Offset for result pagination (skip first N results)

orchestration.description: Deprecated, kept in 1.x: parallel and incremental run the old WorkerPool path on the main thread. On a large app it was no faster than the default path, blocked the server for seconds and took about four times the memory. Leave unset; the default path runs in the scan worker and answers cancellation at once.

parallel.description: Deprecated: runs the old WorkerPool path over the whole program instead of 50 files. Leave unset.

incremental.description: Deprecated: analyzes files changed against baseBranch (requires git, else every file) on the main thread. Leave unset.

baseBranch.description: Git branch to compare against for incremental analysis

maxWorkers.description: Maximum concurrent workers for parallel execution

useWorkerThreads.description: Use worker threads for true multi-core parallelism

tsConfigPath.description: TypeScript config path (auto-detected if not provided)

workerScriptPath.description: Worker script path (auto-detected if not provided)

pluginIds.description: Plugin IDs to load (auto-detected if not provided)

fallbackToWorkers.description: Fallback to worker threads if Promise mode fails

tools.name: scan-architecture
tools.description: Scan Angular codebases for architectural issues with the 17 architecture rules: import cycles (solid:circular-dependency, NG0919 risk), import direction, god objects, layer boundaries, content placement, service bags and more. Returns the violations directly; streaming: true (deprecated) runs in the background instead (poll get-operation-progress); maxResults (default 1000) and resultOffset page the violations; counts cover all of them, summary is a short text.

rootPath.description: Root path of the project to analyze

scope.description: Scope configuration for targeted scanning (apps, libs, modules, features, folders)

names.description: Names of specific projects/features to scan

paths.description: Specific folder paths to scan (for folders type)

rules.description: Specific rules to run (optional, runs all if not specified). Must be exact rule.id values — short names like "circular-dependency" will NOT match. Valid IDs: solid:circular-dependency, solid:import-direction-violation, solid:god-object-violation, architecture:component-complexity, architecture:service-architecture, architecture:content-placement, architecture:advanced-content-placement, architecture:model-separation, architecture:rxjs-memory-leak, architecture:error-handling-pattern, architecture:inheritance-analysis, architecture:performance-pattern, architecture:cross-file-architecture, architecture:service-bag, architecture:static-in-stateful-class, architecture:library-extraction-opportunity, architecture:layer-boundary-violation

includePatterns.description: File patterns to include (optional, defaults to TypeScript files)

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to analyze (default: 100 to prevent memory issues)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of violations to return (pagination)

resultOffset.description: Offset for result pagination (skip first N violations)

orchestration.description: Deprecated, kept in 1.x: parallel and incremental run the old WorkerPool path on the main thread. On a large app it was no faster than the default path, blocked the server for seconds and took about four times the memory. Leave unset; the default path runs in the scan worker and answers cancellation at once.

parallel.description: Deprecated: runs the old WorkerPool path (only with apiStyle imperative). Leave unset.

incremental.description: Deprecated: analyzes files changed against baseBranch (requires git, else every file) on the main thread. Leave unset.

baseBranch.description: Git branch to compare against for incremental analysis

maxWorkers.description: Maximum concurrent workers for parallel execution

enableProgress.description: Enable real-time progress reporting with ETA

useWorkerThreads.description: Use worker threads for true multi-core parallelism

tsConfigPath.description: TypeScript config path (auto-detected if not provided)

workerScriptPath.description: Worker script path (auto-detected if not provided)

pluginIds.description: Plugin IDs to load (auto-detected if not provided)

fallbackToWorkers.description: Fallback to worker threads if Promise mode fails

streaming.description: Deprecated, kept in 1.x (default: false): returns operationId immediately, the analysis runs in the background and get-operation-progress returns the result. Synchronous calls report progress through MCP progress notifications and stop on cancellation.

apiStyle.description: API style to use for analysis execution. "fluent" (default) uses the chainable FluentKernel API with pipeline stages. "imperative" uses traditional Kernel API.

maxDurationMs.description: Time budget in ms, checked between files. When it is reached the scan stops and returns what it has with execution.incomplete = true, the number of skipped files and the slowest rules. 0 disables it. Default 300000 (5 min).

tools.name: scan-solid
tools.description: Scan for SOLID principle violations (DIP, SRP, LSP, OCP, ISP). maxResults (default 1000) and resultOffset page the violations; counts cover all of them, summary is a short text.

rootPath.description: Root path of the project to scan

rules.description: Specific SOLID rules to run (optional, runs all 5 if not specified)

maxFiles.description: Batch size for processing files (default: 100 to prevent memory issues)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of violations to return

tools.name: scan-angular
tools.description: Scan for Angular best practice violations (OnPush, TrackBy, Performance, RxJS, etc.). maxResults (default 1000) and resultOffset page the violations; counts cover all of them, summary is a short text.

rootPath.description: Root path of the project to scan

rules.description: Specific Angular rules to run (optional, runs all 17 if not specified)

maxFiles.description: Batch size for processing files (default: 100 to prevent memory issues)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of violations to return

tools.name: scan-all
tools.description: Comprehensive code quality scan with all plugins (SOLID 7, Angular 28, Architecture 17: 52 rules total). maxResults (default 1000) and resultOffset page the violations; counts cover all of them, summary is a short text.

rootPath.description: Root path of the project to scan

rules.description: Specific rules to run (optional, runs all 52 if not specified)

maxFiles.description: Batch size for processing files (default: 100 to prevent memory issues)

maxResults.description: Maximum number of violations to return

tools.name: compare-health
tools.description: Run the full scan-all scan (all violations, no result window) and compare it with the previous run stored in the project: new, fixed and unchanged violations, per rule (byRule) and per changed file (byFile), plus the lists newViolations and fixedViolations. Violations match by rule, file and message with digits ignored, not by line, so code moving up or down stays unchanged. The first run writes the baseline (status baseline-created). After a comparison the snapshot is replaced by the current run unless updateSnapshot is false. A snapshot taken with other rules or include/exclude patterns is not compared (status scope-mismatch) and is only replaced with updateSnapshot: true. currentRun.bySeverity and byCategory count all violations. Writes only the snapshot file.

rootPath.description: Root path of the project to scan

rules.description: Rule IDs to compare (optional, all 52 if not specified). Part of the snapshot scope.

includePatterns.description: File patterns to include, as in scan-all. Part of the snapshot scope.

excludePatterns.description: File patterns to exclude, as in scan-all. Part of the snapshot scope.

maxFiles.description: Batch size for processing files, as in scan-all.

snapshotPath.description: Snapshot file, absolute or relative to rootPath. Default: .angular-modernizer-cache/health/last-run.json.

updateSnapshot.description: false: compare only, keep the stored snapshot. true: also replace a snapshot with another scope or an unreadable one. Default: replace after a comparison and write the first baseline.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: plan-migration
tools.description: Generate comprehensive, style-aware migration plans for architectural improvements. With projectRoot and file-level violations (filePath, e.g. from scan-architecture, inline or via scanResultFile) the roadmap names concrete files: grouped per file and layer, ordered dependencies first along the import graph, import cycles kept together (planSource "scan"). Without file paths the strategy templates decide the roadmap (planSource "template"). summary is a short text of strategy and roadmap.

filePath.description: File of the violation (absolute or relative to projectRoot). Enables the scan-based plan.

projectRoot.description: Project root with a tsconfig. Required for the scan-based plan (import graph and layers from layers / layersSource).

scanResultFile.description: Saved scan-architecture result ({ violations: [...] }, a violation array, or the MCP text content) to read violations from. Absolute or relative to projectRoot. Replaces or extends violations.

maxResults.description: Scan-based plan: at most this many files per phase and violations per file (phases and files are marked truncated; counts cover everything). Default 25. Ignored by the template plan.

maxPhases.description: Upper bound for scan-based phases; consecutive dependency levels are merged beyond it. Default 6.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

orchestration.description: Phase 6d/7b orchestration options (subset for migration planning)

enableProgress.description: Enable real-time progress reporting for complex migration planning

styleProfile.description: Codebase style profile from learn-patterns tool

filterStyleConflicts.description: Filter out migration steps that conflict with codebase style

tools.name: transform-code
tools.description: Apply surgical code transformations to fix architectural issues. summary is a short text with the outcome, the changes, the type check, backup and rollback.

filePath.description: Path to the file to transform (single file mode)

files.description: Paths to multiple files to transform (batch mode)

options.description: Transformation-specific options. service-bag-transform: assignments ({ methodName: groupKey }) moves methods into the named group (e.g. uncertain methods from the scan metadata); unassigned uncertain methods stay in the original service

validateBeforeTransform.description: Whether to validate before transformation (default: true)

createBackup.description: Whether to create a backup before transformation (default: true)

validateTransformation.description: Whether to validate transformation results (default: true): type check of the transformed file (new errors only; in a batch every batch file, a file with a new error fails and rollbackStrategy applies), plus build and lint when enabled

autoRollback.description: Whether to automatically rollback on validation failure (default: true)

rollbackStrategy.description: Rollback strategy for batch operations, applied when a file fails (transformation error or introduced type error): all-or-nothing restores every file, selective the failed ones, none nothing

orchestration.description: Orchestration options for parallel and incremental transformations. Note: parallel defaults to false for safety.

parallel.description: Enable parallel transformation processing (batch mode only). Defaults to FALSE for safety.

useWorkerThreads.description: Use worker threads for parallel transformations (Phase 6d). Requires tsConfigPath and workerScriptPath.

autoSelectMode.description: Enable intelligent auto-selection of Promise vs Worker mode based on project complexity. Defaults to true when parallel is enabled.

maxWorkers.description: Maximum number of parallel workers. Default: auto-selected based on CPU cores and memory.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for parallel operations. Default: 30000.

maxMemory.description: Maximum memory usage in bytes. Triggers throttling when exceeded.

maxWorkers.description: Maximum concurrent workers regardless of system capacity.

pluginIds.description: Plugin IDs to load for worker thread transformations.

streaming.description: Deprecated, kept in 1.x (default: false): returns operationId immediately, the transformation runs in the background with the same backup, validation and rollback, and get-operation-progress returns its result once completed. Synchronous calls report progress through MCP progress notifications and roll back when cancelled.

diffFormat.description: No effect: streaming runs the regular transformation in the background and emits no diff events. Kept so existing calls stay valid.

apiStyle.description: API style to use for transformation execution. "fluent" (default) uses the chainable FluentKernel API with pipeline stages. "imperative" uses traditional Kernel API.

buildCheck.description: Enable build validation after transformation (fluent API only). Validates that the transformation did not break the build.

validateBuild.description: Whether to run the project build after transformation (default: false). The transformed file is type-checked either way and rolled back on new type errors; the build runs build.command of .angular-modernizer.json (or the detected build system) and can take minutes on a large app.

validateLint.description: Whether to run the project's lint script after transformation (default: false). Lints the whole project; the transformed file is type-checked either way and rolled back on new type errors.

rollbackOnBuildFailure.description: Whether to automatically rollback on build failure (default: true). When enabled, restores backups if build validation fails.

buildTimeout.description: Build validation timeout in milliseconds (default: 300000 = 5 minutes).

projectRoot.description: Project root path for build validation. If not provided, will be auto-detected from filePath.

tools.name: run-angular-cli
tools.description: Execute Angular CLI commands for project management and code generation. The result has the full stdout and stderr; summary is a short text with the exit code and, on failure, the last output lines.

tools.name: run-build
tools.description: Execute build systems to validate code transformations. Supports incremental mode for 2-4x faster builds by validating only changed files and their dependencies. Automatically detects incompatibilities and falls back to full build when needed. The result has the full build output; summary is a short text with the outcome, the build mode and, on failure, the last output lines.

incrementalMode.description: Enable incremental build mode (default: true). Auto-detects changed files and validates only affected code for 2-4x faster builds.

changedFiles.description: List of changed files to validate (optional, auto-detected from git if not provided)

forceFullBuild.description: Force full build even if incremental is available

tools.name: analyze-core-to-shared
tools.description: Analyze core-to-shared dependency violations with impact assessment. counts cover all violations, summary is a short text with the most imported shared modules and the first violations.

rootPath.description: Root path of the project to analyze

includeImpactAssessment.description: Whether to include impact assessment (reverse dependencies, breaking change risk)

maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files to analyze (for performance)

maxWorkers.description: Maximum parallel workers for impact assessment

resourceLimits.description: Resource limits for large codebase analysis

tools.name: run-schematic
tools.description: Execute Angular schematics for code generation and automated migrations. The result has the full stdout and stderr; summary is a short text with the outcome, the generated files and, on failure, the last output lines.

target.description: Target path or name for the generated artifact

skipPrompts.description: Skip interactive prompts (passes --interactive=false to ng generate)

dryRun.description: Perform a dry run without writing files

tools.name: validate-before-transform
tools.description: Validate code before transformation to ensure it is safe to modify. Performs syntax, dependency, type, and schema validation. summary is a short text with the verdict, the issue counts and the first issues.

filePath.description: Path to the file to validate

validateSyntax.description: Whether to perform syntax validation (default: true)

validateDependencies.description: Whether to perform dependency validation (default: true)

validateTypes.description: Whether to perform type validation (default: true)

validateSchema.description: Whether to perform schema validation (default: false). Requires schema parameter.

schema.description: Optional schema for transformation-specific validation. Example: { requiresClass: true, requiresDecorator: "Component" }

tools.name: validate-transformation
tools.description: Validate code after transformation to ensure changes did not break anything. Supports incremental build mode for 2-4x faster validation by checking only transformed files and their dependencies. Automatically detects project compatibility and falls back to full validation when needed. summary is a short text with the verdict, the validation mode, the issue counts and the first issues.

filePath.description: Path to the file to validate (or project root for batch validation)

validateBuild.description: Whether to perform build validation (default: true)

validateTests.description: Whether to perform test validation (default: false). Tests can be slow.

validateLint.description: Whether to perform lint validation (default: true)

cwd.description: Working directory for command execution (default: auto-detect)

incrementalMode.description: Enable incremental build mode (default: true). Auto-detects transformed files and validates only affected code for 2-4x faster validation.

transformedFiles.description: List of transformed files to validate (optional, auto-detected from git if not provided)

forceFullBuild.description: Force full validation even if incremental is available

tools.name: rollback-changes
tools.description: Rollback transformations if validation fails or changes are unsatisfactory. Restores the backups transform-code wrote into <projectRoot>/.angular-modernizer-backups (file copies, plus a git snapshot inside a git repository); without files it restores the files of the last transform-code call. summary is a short text with the outcome and the restored files.

files.description: Specific files to rollback (optional - restores the files of the last transform-code call if not specified)

strategy.description: Rollback strategy: "auto" (file backup first, then the git snapshot), "git-stash" (git snapshot recorded by transform-code; never applies a stash from the stash list), or "file-backup"

backupDir.description: Custom backup directory for file backups (optional - defaults to <projectRoot>/.angular-modernizer-backups)

projectRoot.description: Project root (optional - defaults to gitRoot, else the nearest folder with tsconfig.json, package.json or .angular-modernizer.json above the first file)

gitRoot.description: Git project root (optional - used as project root when projectRoot is not given)

tools.name: learn-patterns
tools.description: Discover recurring architectural patterns, anti-patterns and transformation opportunities in a codebase with AST heuristics (RxJS, components, services, transformations, architecture), count their occurrences and store them in a pattern knowledge base that later runs extend. Detects the codebase style conventions. summary is a short text of patterns and style profile.

targetPath.description: Path to the codebase to learn patterns from

outputPath.description: Custom output path for generated artifacts

crossValidateWithExisting.description: Whether to cross-validate with existing rules

enableLearning.description: Enable self-learning: persist patterns for future scans

knowledgeBasePath.description: Path to pattern knowledge base file (default: .angular-modernizer-cache/pattern-knowledge.json)

compareWithPreviousScan.description: Compare with previous scan results to track pattern evolution

respectCodebaseStyle.description: Align patterns with existing codebase style conventions

generateStyleProfile.description: Auto-detect and generate style profile (RxJS, DI, state management)

generateRules.description: Generate analysis rules from high-confidence patterns

ruleOutputPath.description: Output path for generated rule files

filterRulesByStyle.description: Only generate rules that align with codebase style

enableProgress.description: Enable real-time progress reporting during pattern discovery

maxWorkers.description: Maximum parallel workers for file analysis

resourceLimits.description: Resource limits for large codebase analysis

tools.name: get-operation-progress
tools.description: Deprecated, kept in 1.x: polls an operation started with streaming: true (transform-code, scan-architecture). Call those tools synchronously instead: they send MCP progress notifications when the request has a progressToken and stop on notifications/cancelled. Get progress for a streaming operation (transformation or analysis). Returns status, events, and operation metadata including diffs and syntax errors. A completed operation carries the tool result in result; summary is a short text with the status, the last event and the result summary.

operationId.description: Unique operation identifier from streaming transformation/analysis

sinceTimestamp.description: Only return events after this timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)

tools.name: check-incremental-compatibility
tools.description: Check if a project is compatible with incremental build validation. Detects blockers like circular dependencies, old Angular versions, custom build configs, and complex monorepos. Returns compatibility status, issues, recommendations, and estimated speedup. summary is a short text with the verdict, the recommendation and the detected issues.

projectPath.description: Project root path to check for incremental build compatibility

maxCircularDeps.description: Maximum circular dependency chains before blocking (default: 10)

maxInterProjectDeps.description: Maximum inter-project dependencies in monorepo before warning (default: 20)

tools.name: analyze-build-impact
tools.description: Analyze build impact before transformations. Estimates affected files, transitive dependents, Angular modules, build time, and provides clear recommendations for AI usage. Helps determine if a transformation is safe to proceed. External .html templates are mapped to their component files. Host components that use a changed component, directive or pipe only in their template (NgModule declarations) are listed as templateHosts. The recommendation and counts come first, summary repeats them as text; use summaryOnly to skip the file lists or maxResults to cap them.

filesToChange.description: Array of file paths that will be changed (relative to project root or absolute). These files are the changed set.

symbols.description: Optional exported symbol names of the changed files. When given, only consumers of exactly these symbols count as dependents, and symbolImpacts lists value / type-only consumers per symbol.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: validate-project-compatibility
tools.description: Validate project compatibility with the parser before running transformations. Detects incompatibility patterns such as external decorators, path aliases, and complex constructor patterns. Returns project type, compatibility status, recommended parser, estimated success rate, and actionable recommendations. Prevents wasted effort on transformation tests that will fail. Completes in <5 seconds. summary is a short text with the verdict, the parser and the failed checks.

projectPath.description: Project root path to validate for parser compatibility

maxSampleSize.description: Maximum number of files to sample for detection (default: 50)

runSampleTest.description: Whether to run sample transformation test (default: true)

sampleTestTimeout.description: Timeout for sample transformation test in milliseconds (default: 5000)

tools.name: collect-feedback
tools.description: Manually collect transformation feedback for AI learning. Stores feedback in <projectRoot>/.claude-feedback, plus the platform store when ANGULAR_MODERNIZER_PLATFORM_ROOT is set. Validates feedback, anonymizes file paths, and extracts learnings automatically. Use kind 'analysis' to report a read-only tool result (find-usages, search-codebase, scans) that had to be corrected by grep, build output, a script or manual reading; 'analysis' accepts one record or an array and needs no execution/duration/build data. summary is a short text with what was stored and the validation issues.

projectRoot.description: Project root path (defaults to process.cwd() if not provided)

sessionId.description: Optional session ID (existing session or create new)

kind.description: Record kind (default: 'transformation'). 'transformation' requires transformation + execution; 'analysis' requires analysis.

analysis.description: Analysis record or array of records (kind 'analysis'). Each: tool, claimed, actual, fallbackUsed, optional query/evidence/impact/category.

query.description: Query passed to the tool (args object or text)

fallbackUsed.description: How the truth was established: 'grep' | 'build' | 'script' | 'manual' | 'none' or another short label

query.description: Query passed to the tool (args object or text)

fallbackUsed.description: How the truth was established: 'grep' | 'build' | 'script' | 'manual' | 'none' or another short label

error.description: Optional error message if execution failed

errorType.description: Optional error classification (build, type, lint, test, runtime, ...). Inferred from error text when omitted.

buildErrors.description: Optional build error messages (e.g. 'NG8001: app-x is not a known element'); used as learning evidence

storageLocation.description: Where to store feedback (default 'both'). Feedback always goes to <projectRoot>/.claude-feedback; 'both' adds the platform store only when ANGULAR_MODERNIZER_PLATFORM_ROOT is set, 'platform' requires that variable.

tools.name: review-feedback
tools.description: Review collected feedback and extract insights for AI learning. Reads <projectRoot>/.claude-feedback, plus the platform store when ANGULAR_MODERNIZER_PLATFORM_ROOT is set. Detects success patterns, failure patterns, quality trends, and outliers. summary is a short text with the counts, the success rate, the top insights and the quality warnings.

projectRoot.description: Project root path (defaults to process.cwd() if not provided)

sessionId.description: Optional session ID (specific session or all sessions)

since.description: Optional date filter: ISO 8601 date or date-time, e.g. 2026-10-01 (feedback from then on)

source.description: Where to read feedback from (default 'both'): <projectRoot>/.claude-feedback, plus the platform store when ANGULAR_MODERNIZER_PLATFORM_ROOT is set; 'platform' requires that variable.

tool.description: Optional tool filter for analysis records (e.g. 'find-usages')

tools.name: suggest-improvements
tools.description: Suggest rule adjustments based on feedback analysis. Analyzes transformation outcomes to identify improvement opportunities: parameter adjustments, prerequisite checks, approach changes, validation enhancements. All suggestions require human approval. summary is a short text with the data points, the current performance and the top suggestions.

projectRoot.description: Project root path (defaults to process.cwd() if not provided)

ruleId.description: Rule identifier to analyze (e.g., 'standalone-migration', 'constructor-to-inject'), or an analysis tool name (e.g. 'find-usages') to get blind-spot suggestions from kind 'analysis' feedback

source.description: Where to read feedback from (default 'both'): <projectRoot>/.claude-feedback, plus the platform store when ANGULAR_MODERNIZER_PLATFORM_ROOT is set; 'platform' requires that variable.

tools.name: analyze-parser-performance
tools.description: Analyze parser performance metrics from transformation feedback sessions. Generates actionable improvement recommendations based on parser behavior. Reads <projectRoot>/.claude-feedback, plus the platform store when ANGULAR_MODERNIZER_PLATFORM_ROOT is set. Supports multi-session aggregation. summary is a short text of the metrics and the top suggestions.

projectRoot.description: Project root path (defaults to process.cwd() if not provided)

sessionIds.description: Optional session IDs to analyze (defaults to all sessions with parser metadata)

source.description: Where to read feedback from (default 'both'): <projectRoot>/.claude-feedback, plus the platform store when ANGULAR_MODERNIZER_PLATFORM_ROOT is set; 'platform' requires that variable.

tools.name: extract-libraries
tools.description: Detect Angular artifacts in shared folders that qualify for extraction into dedicated libraries with secondary entry points. Returns opportunities with cohesion/reusability scores and suggested library names; counts cover all of them, summary is a short text.

rootPath.description: Root path of the Angular project to analyze

targetFolders.description: Folders to scan for extraction candidates. Default: ['shared', 'common', 'core', 'libs', 'models', 'interfaces', 'projects']

minReusabilityScore.description: Minimum reusability score (0-100) to qualify as a candidate. Default: 40

minCohesionScore.description: Minimum cohesion score (0-1) for an artifact cluster. Default: 0.5

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 1000

excludePatterns.description: Glob patterns to exclude from scanning (e.g. ["**/generated/**"])

tools.name: parse-stack-trace
tools.description: Parse a Node.js/Angular/Zone.js/browser stack trace into structured frames. Maps each frame to its source file, line, column, and function name. Classifies frames as project files or external dependencies (node_modules). Browser frames (http://host/src/..., webpack:///, ng:///, bare file names) are mapped onto project files via resolvedFile; an ambiguous file name lists candidates. Use as the first step in bug investigation when a stack trace is available.

stackTrace.description: Raw stack trace string from Error.stack, console output, or test runner.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root for classifying project vs. external frames.

projectFramesOnly.description: When true, only project frames are returned. Defaults to false.

tools.name: find-usages
tools.description: Find all references to a symbol (class, method, function, variable, or constant) across a TypeScript project. Returns file paths, line numbers, source snippets, and usage type: read/write/call/argument/decorator-argument (resolved references), declaration (the name of the declaring class, method, property or interface member), template (Angular template usage: component/directive selector, pipe name, member read/call/write, input/output binding; external templateUrl and inline templates; templateMatch is "verified" or "template-unverified" for same-name matches that could not be tied to the symbol), and unresolved (same-name identifiers whose symbol does not resolve, e.g. a class still used after its import was removed). The file option filters reported usages only. Use after parse-stack-trace to trace call paths and determine blast radius before proposing a bug fix. countsByType and countsByDirectory always cover all usages; use summaryOnly for a quick overview of widely used symbols, maxResults to cap the list.

symbol.description: Symbol name to search for (class, method, function, variable, constant).

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

file.description: Only report usages located in this file (absolute path, .ts or .html). The symbol declaration may live in any file. Optional.

usageType.description: Restrict results to this usage type. `call` is only the callee; `inject(Foo)` is `argument`, `@ViewChild(Foo)` is `decorator-argument`. Optional.

includeTemplates.description: Include Angular template usages (selectors, pipes, member reads/calls, bindings). Defaults to true.

includeUnresolved.description: Include same-name identifiers that do not resolve to any symbol (e.g. missing import, TS2304). Defaults to true.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: get-call-graph
tools.description: Build a caller/callee graph for a named method, function, constructor, get/set accessor or arrow-function property. Direction "up" shows who calls it, "down" shows what it calls, "both" returns the full call tree. Configurable depth (default: 2). Prefer "ClassName.method" and the narrowest direction you need. The graph is capped at maxNodes (default 200); a capped result has truncated: true. Callers are not expanded through Angular lifecycle hooks or interface members of foreign classes (set includeLifecycleHooks to override). summaryOnly returns counts and direct neighbours only. Callees are resolved via the type checker and include new X() (constructor incl. field initializers), super(), and property reads that resolve to getters. Callers of component members include calls from the component template as leaf nodes (kind "template", template file and line, snippet), also from templates of subclasses that inherit the member (className of the subclass, inheritedFrom of the declaring class; a subclass overriding it is left out). Use method "ClassName.constructor" to see what runs transitively during construction. Use after parse-stack-trace to trace error propagation through the call hierarchy.

method.description: Name of the callable to analyse: method, function, get/set accessor, arrow-function property, "constructor", or class-qualified ("ClassName.member", "ClassName.constructor").

file.description: Absolute path of the source file containing the method.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

tools.name: inspect-template
tools.description: Inspect an Angular component template (.html file, or the component .ts for inline templates). Per element: tag, line, control-flow depth, bindings (input, output, two-way, attribute, structural, reference with their expressions) and the project components/directives whose selector matches it. Per template: components/directives used (with files), pipes (resolved to project pipe classes when declared in the project), custom elements without a project match (library components), control-flow blocks, structural directives and max nesting depth, and static i18n keys (translate pipe/directive, i18n="@@id"), plus the static prefixes of dynamic keys ('A.' + x, `A.${x}`) in dynamicI18nPrefixes (definitions and project-wide usages of a key: inspect-i18n). Plain elements without bindings are omitted unless includePlainElements; counts always cover all elements. summaryOnly drops the element, key and prefix lists, maxResults caps them.

file.description: Template .html file or component .ts file (absolute, or relative to projectRoot).

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

includePlainElements.description: Also list elements without bindings, references or directive matches. Default: false.

tools.name: find-component-hosts
tools.description: Find every component template that uses a component or directive (by className or selector) and report per host: template file, element occurrences with line, which of the target's inputs and outputs are bound or unbound, required inputs that are missing, and bindings no matched project directive declares (native events, library directives, typos). coverage lists per input/output which hosts bind it and which do not (e.g. "which hosts ignore (formError)?"). Inputs/outputs come from @Input/@Output (aliases, required), signal input(), input.required(), model(), output(), decorator inputs/outputs arrays and base classes. Test hosts in spec files are skipped unless includeTestHosts. dynamicHosts lists places creating a component in code: any call or new whose parameter takes a component type (MatDialog.open, createComponent, ComponentPortal, project dialog wrappers), with sink, via (wrapper chain down to the library call), resolution (literal, variable, field, di-token, method-return, callback, selector, lazy-import, registry, promise), the other arguments (data) and what the caller does with the result (e.g. afterClosed.subscribe; a stored result shows the use that subscribes to it). Route entries (component, loadComponent) are dynamic hosts with route: path joined over children, guards, data, resolve, lazy. candidateHosts lists places that may create it: lookups in a component registry (e.g. dynamicComponents) whose selector comes from data (selectorExpression, selectorLiterals); a selector fixed by literals, a switch mapping or an equality guard is decided (dynamicHosts or nothing). includeDynamic: false skips both. For result and data flow of a dialog use trace-output-flow. For widely used components start with summaryOnly (counts per input/output only). summaryOnly drops the host list, maxResults caps it and the host names in coverage; counts (incl. coverage bound/unbound) always cover all hosts.

className.description: Class name of the component or directive. Give className or selector.

selector.description: Selector of the component or directive, e.g. "app-item" or "[appTooltip]". Give className or selector.

file.description: File declaring the class (absolute, or relative to projectRoot). Picks one of several same-name classes. Optional.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

includeOccurrences.description: Include per-element occurrences with line and bindings. Default: true.

includeTestHosts.description: Also report test host components declared in *.spec.ts / *.test.ts. Default: false.

includeDynamic.description: Also find places creating the component in code (dialogs, createComponent, wrappers) as dynamicHosts. Default: true.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: trace-output-flow
tools.description: Follow the payload of a component's or directive's @Output across the template boundary, where get-call-graph stops. Per output: kind (EventEmitter, output(), model(), outputFromObservable, Subject) and payload type; every emit site (emit/next, model set/update) with the enclosing method and the emitted expression; every host template that binds it with the handler expression, the host method the handler calls, which argument carries $event, and what that method does with the value: writes (p.disabled = evt), calls passing it on (followed into the callee up to depth), re-emits, conditions, returns. Hosts that use the component without binding the output are listed as unboundIn; eventUnused marks handlers that drop the payload. For a component created in code (dialog, createComponent, wrapper) the dynamic section is the same question for its result: dataInjections (what it injects from the creating library, e.g. MAT_DIALOG_DATA), closeSites (ref.close(value)) and per creation site the result chain (afterClosed.subscribe) with the handler receiving the result and its effects: callback parameter, observer next, the local of an awaited firstValueFrom, the handler after a switchMap/concatMap/mergeMap/exhaustMap (handler.via); handler.resultUnused when it never reads the result; a returned result lists its callers (two levels) in forwardedTo; result.note says why a result is not followed (toSignal, portal attach, no callers). Route entries are listed with path and guards. Subscriptions in code outside the target (ref.instance.x.subscribe, dialogRef.componentInstance.x.pipe(...).subscribe, a viewChild field) are listed per output as subscribedIn with the handler and its effects, like a dynamic result. For widely used components start with summaryOnly. summaryOnly drops emit sites, host and subscription lists and the dynamic lists, maxResults caps them per output and per dynamic list; counts always cover everything.

className.description: Class name of the component or directive. Give className or selector.

selector.description: Selector of the component or directive, e.g. "app-item". Give className or selector.

file.description: File declaring the class (absolute, or relative to projectRoot). Picks one of several same-name classes. Optional.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

depth.description: Callables to walk per $event argument: 1 = the handler method only, 2 = also the methods it passes the value to. Default: 2, max: 5.

includeTestHosts.description: Also report test host components declared in *.spec.ts / *.test.ts. Default: false.

includeDynamic.description: Also trace creation in code (dialogs, createComponent, wrappers): data injected, close sites, result handlers, route entries (the dynamic section). Registry candidates with a data selector stay in find-component-hosts. Default: true.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: get-bootstrap-execution
tools.description: List what an Angular app executes at startup and whether it touches a given expression. Roots: provideAppInitializer/provideEnvironmentInitializer/providePlatformInitializer and APP_INITIALIZER-style provider literals (timing "initializer", finish before "bootstrap"), bootstrapApplication/bootstrapModule ("bootstrap"), HTTP_INTERCEPTORS classes and withInterceptors functions ("first-http-request", can happen inside an initializer that uses HttpClient), other useFactory providers ("first-injection"). From each root it walks calls (incl. constructors, field initializers, getters) and DI: inject(X), constructor parameters, @Inject(TOKEN) and factory deps, with tokens resolved to the providers registered in the project. watch (e.g. ["AppConfig.settings"]) reports every reachable read/write with the call path from the root, which catches reads hidden behind constructors and getters that search-codebase cannot see. method + file start from one callable instead (e.g. "AuthInterceptor.constructor"). Roots are found by scanning source files, not by evaluating which providers are registered; spec files are skipped. Start with summaryOnly; maxResults caps the reached list per root and the watch hits.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

watch.description: Expressions whose reads and writes to report, matched by text (optional chaining ignored), e.g. ["AppConfig.settings"].

timings.description: Only roots with these timings. Default: all.

file.description: Only roots registered in this file; with method, the file declaring it (absolute, or relative to projectRoot).

method.description: Start from this callable instead of the discovered roots: "Class.constructor", "Class.member" or a function name. Needs file.

depth.description: Maximum call/injection distance from a root. Default: 8.

maxNodes.description: Maximum callables walked per root; a capped root is marked truncated. Default: 300.

includeReached.description: Include the reached callables per root. Default: true.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: inspect-form-group
tools.description: Inspect the Reactive Forms of a component or service file. Per form property: the control tree (dotted paths, FormArray items as "[]", kind, validators, async validators, created disabled, added via addControl) and every call in the file that changes a control: enable, disable, set/add/remove/clear validators, setErrors, updateValueAndValidity, add/remove/setControl (value changes with includeValueOperations), resolved through controls.x, controls["x"], get("a.b"), get([...]), at(i), local variables and getters. cascade lists enable()/disable() on ancestor groups that also switch the control; reEnabledBy flags controls disabled on purpose that an ancestor enable() switches back on. unknownPaths lists paths that do not exist in the form (typos, stale names: a runtime error when called); dynamicOperations lists computed keys (controls[key] in a loop). Only this file is searched. summaryOnly drops the control lists, maxResults caps them.

file.description: The .ts file declaring the form (absolute, or relative to projectRoot).

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

className.description: Only this class of the file. Optional.

form.description: Only this form property, e.g. "formGroup". Optional.

includeValueOperations.description: Also report setValue, patchValue, reset, valueChanges, statusChanges. Default: false.

includeCascade.description: Include the ancestor enable()/disable() list per control. Default: true.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

tools.name: inspect-i18n
tools.description: Translation keys (ngx-translate, transloco) of a project: where a key is defined per language (file, line, value), where it is used (templates: translate pipe/directive, i18n="@@id"; code: TranslateService instant/get/stream, TranslocoService translate/selectTranslate, keys resolved through constants, ternaries and helpers), and which languages lack it. Sources are found without configuration: objects passed to setTranslation (followed through variables, imports, rest parameters, forEach and lookups like MAP[customer]), JSON folders of TranslateHttpLoader or a TranslocoLoader URL, else assets/i18n/*.json. Sources reached through a runtime lookup or a branch are conditional (customer overlays, grouped by lookup key). Each app of a workspace (folder with tsconfig.app.json) has its own layers (languages: base, groups, "<app>:base"); missingIn compares a key with the languages of each layer defining it, never an overlay key against the base; overlay values of base keys are marked overrides. A usage counts as defined only by sources of its own app (library code: any app). With key or prefix: keys[] with definitions, usages, missingIn, coveredBy, referencedAt. Without: project report with undefinedKeys (used, defined nowhere), missingTranslations, unused, dynamicPrefixes ('A.' + x, `A.${x}`) and unresolvedUsages (key fully dynamic). "Unused" cannot be proven statically: status covered-by-dynamic (a dynamic prefix covers it), referenced-as-literal (the key text appears as a string elsewhere, e.g. a menu config) or no-static-usage. For a project report start with summaryOnly (drops the lists and the source details registeredAt, discoveredBy, kind, conditionReason); maxResults caps every list and the usages per key, counts cover everything.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

key.description: Report this translation key only, e.g. "ERRORS.NO_ACCESS_TITLE". Optional.

prefix.description: Report the keys starting with this text, e.g. "ERRORS.". Optional; not with key.

i18nNames.description: Pipe and attribute-directive names that take a translation key. Default: ["translate", "transloco"].

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: find-angular-symbol
tools.description: Find Angular symbols (components, directives, pipes, services, guards, interceptors, resolvers, modules, tokens) by selector, pipe name, or class name. Accepts CSS selectors (e.g. app-user), attribute selectors (e.g. appHighlight), pipe template names (e.g. dateFormat), or TypeScript class names. Supports standard Angular decorators and the project component decorators listed in parser.componentDecorators of .angular-modernizer.json. Library components, directives and pipes (e.g. the ngx-translate translate pipe) come from compiled .d.ts metadata with source "library", after project symbols; they match exactly (class name, pipe name or one selector of the list), not by substring. *.spec.ts files are skipped. Use during bug investigation to locate which class owns a given selector or pipe. Selector and pipe queries match substrings; use summaryOnly or maxResults for short queries.

query.description: Selector, pipe name, or class name to search for. CSS selectors (app-user), attribute selectors (appHighlight), pipe names (dateFormat), or class names (UserComponent) are all valid.

type.description: Optional. Limit results to this symbol type. Omit to search all types.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: search-codebase
tools.description: Search TypeScript source files in a project. Three modes: "text" (literal substring), "pattern" (regular expression), "symbol" (TypeScript class/function/interface/enum/type declaration by name). Returns file path, line, column, and source snippet for each match. Text and pattern modes also scan Angular templates (.html) and .ts files outside the tsconfig program (e.g. src/i18n/*.ts) under projectRoot, skipping node_modules, dist, .angular, coverage and hidden directories. The response includes a coverage object (programFileCount, extraFileCount); 0 hits only prove absence within the covered files. Use during bug investigation to locate error strings, find symbol declarations, or discover all files that reference a specific pattern.

query.description: The text, regex pattern, or TypeScript symbol name to search for.

mode.description: "text" - literal substring match. "pattern" - regular expression match. "symbol" - finds TypeScript named declarations (class, function, interface, enum, type alias, variable).

projectRoot.description: Absolute path to the project root. Must contain a tsconfig.json.

include.description: Optional glob pattern to limit which files are searched, e.g. "**/*.service.ts".

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 100.

includeTemplates.description: Text/pattern modes: also scan .html templates under projectRoot. Defaults to true.

includeNonProgramFiles.description: Text/pattern modes: also scan .ts files under projectRoot that are not part of the tsconfig program (e.g. src/i18n/*.ts). Defaults to true.

tools.name: verify-citations
tools.description: Check the path:line citations of Markdown plans (bug-fix plans, feature plans, investigation reports) against the current code. Per citation: ok (the symbol named next to it is inside the cited range), unverified (range exists, no symbol to check; current line text shown), moved (symbol found at other lines: foundAt), anchor-missing (symbol nowhere in the file), out-of-range (file too short), missing-file (similar files listed as candidates), ambiguous (bare file name matches several files). Citations inside fenced code blocks are skipped. Run before executing a plan and after writing one. needsAttention counts moved, anchor-missing, out-of-range, missing-file and ambiguous; those come first in citations. Read-only.

planPaths.description: Markdown files to check, absolute or relative to projectRoot (e.g. plan.md and investigation.md of one plan folder).

projectRoot.description: Absolute path of the repository the plans cite. Cited paths resolve from here, then from the plan folder, then by path suffix.

summaryOnly.description: Return counts and the text summary only, without the result list. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Return at most this many list entries; the result is then marked truncated and counts still describe the full result. Default: no limit.

tools.name: server-status
tools.description: Report on the running MCP server itself: pid, parent pid, uptime, memory (RSS, heap), the ts-morph projects in the shared cache (tsconfig path, source file count, heap taken at load, load and last-use time, source files re-read after a change on disk), the cache limits (projects, heap MB) and evictions (count, last one with reason and heap/RSS before and after), response sizes (count, last, largest, oversized responses replaced by an error), and whether a package dist/ was rebuilt after the server started. When build.rebuiltSinceStart is true this session still runs the old code: reconnect the MCP server to load the new build. Use it when results look stale, before measuring response sizes, or when memory grows.
